claim_a: The EU produces only 9% of the soy protein it consumes, so about 91% is imported (PPE-03, citing JRC and Profundo)
claim_b: 94% of soya used in the EU is imported (European Commission Action Plan COM(2026)355, as recorded in PSB-009 from VIS-15)
position_taken: Keep VIS-15 for the benchmark row PSB-009; the bases differ (soy protein including food against soya volume). Do not average. Not used in any Vietnamese figure

topic: Concentration of EU soy import origins
claim_a: 86% of EU soy imports come from Brazil, Argentina and the United States (PPE-03, citing Kuepper and Stravens 2022)
claim_b: 85% of EU soya imports come from Brazil and the United States alone (PPE-05, citing the same 2022 source)
position_taken: Unresolved: two publications by the same organisation cite one source for different country sets. Not used in the study
notes: Shows the publications need checking against primary data before reuse

topic: Business-as-usual change in EU soy protein imports to 2035
claim_a: Figure 6 of PPE-03 labels the business-as-usual result as minus 1%
claim_b: The same figure shows 15.1 Mt in 2025 and 14.62 Mt in 2035, minus 3.2% (our calculation)
position_taken: Use the tonnages (15.1 to 14.62 Mt) and report minus 3.2%, marked as our calculation
notes: Internal inconsistency in the source; also 1-in-8 and 1-in-6 rotation assumptions appear in different places of PPE-04

topic: Scale of the EU fava bean roadmap consultation
claim_a: Developed with 20 value-chain actors and 60+ experts (PPE-05, executive summary)
claim_b: 19 taskforce stakeholders plus over 90 expert consultations (PPE-05, section 1.2)
position_taken: Report 19 taskforce organisations and over 90 consultations, the more detailed statement, and note the other
notes: Minor; affects only how the method is described
